body: GHA currently fails because godot-cpp doesn't recognize these new bindings, ironically demonstrating that the new binding metadata works

Thanks a lot for experimenting further on this front! :slightly_smiling_face: 

> Because the prospect of changing the formatting of the entire codebase for supporting a nullable type is daunting, this aims to take a more hands-off approach by adding non-null metadata to bindings exclusively.

Doesn't this run the risk that it's very difficult to keep it in sync with actual method signatures? One can easily forget to update nullability information in a bind, and things will keep compiling, but advertise wrong signatures in GDExtension.

Regarding "daunting", personally I believe we should rather approach this slowly, but properly. Meaning I'd be absolutely fine with 4.5 only shipping a handful of _required_ signatures, and we can continuously extend this over time. This effort has to be done either way (with binds or with signatures), and the big part of the work is likely finding out where nulls are allowed -- not changing `RequiredPtr<T>` in the function declaration.

The original approach https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86079 would still allow us to solve two problems at once:
1. We have the confidence that the GDExtension bindings reflect actual semantics in C++ code
2. C++ code _itself_ also benefits from additional type safety

> Doesn't this run the risk that it's very difficult to keep it in sync with actual method signatures? One can easily forget to update nullability information in a bind, and things will keep compiling, but advertise wrong signatures in GDExtension.

That's the tradeoff of this non-invasive implementation, which is more about getting the metadata as a concept passed onto GDExtension. There's a partial workaround that's still somewhat non-invasive but still requires manual validation, which is implementing a dummy wrapper around the types we want to require:
```cpp
template <typename T>
using Required = T;
...
Required<Node> *some_function(const Required<Ref<Resource>> &p_some_argument);
static_assert(std::is_same_v<Node *, Required<Node> *>)
static_assert(std::is_same_v<Ref<Resource>, Required<Ref<Resource>>>)
```
C++ lacks distinguishing between `typedefs`, so the manual binding annotations would be needed, but this is ultimately a temporary measure to convey intent. Still, this was made with speed of implementation in mind, which doesn't sound like what you're interested in.

> The original approach https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86079 would still allow us to solve two problems at once:
> 1. We have the confidence that the GDExtension bindings reflect actual semantics in C++ code
> 2. C++ code itself also benefits from additional type safety

Snopek's design indeed feels the most suitable so far. While I'm not 100% sold on that implementation (which is probably why it's still a draft), if we're keeping this as something object-specific then I'll try to take heavier inspiration from it. Knowing that this is something "okay" to give a slower but more involved approach should make things easier as well, as I can start digging into more invasive implementations that have more guarantees of safety, but without the need for SFINAE shenanigans that my first idea had because this'd be *specific* to objects.

> Snopek's design indeed feels the most suitable so far. While I'm not 100% sold on that implementation (which is probably why it's still a draft), if we're keeping this as something object-specific then I'll try to take heavier inspiration from it.

Could you maybe express concrete criticism/shortcomings on the current implementation in #86079, ideally as a review of that PR? To me it's not quite clear what requirements an ideal solution from your perspective would have :slightly_smiling_face:

Because if that PR comes already close, then it might be more efficient to iterate on that (whether it's you or David adding more commits) rather than starting again from scratch. That said, showcasing different approaches was insightful too, so thanks a lot for that :+1: maybe we can take the best of all worlds...
